title: Choose the visual world for AgentOps AI
question: The roll assigned Custody Record. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Custody Record
options.lineage: forensic chain-of-custody tags and evidence logs
options.thesis: Every answer is evidence: case-numbered, its custody chain signed at every handoff.
options.viewport: Manila nav rail; the run as case EX-7A41 with its custody chain streaming across the top, the answer and numbered exhibits beside it.
options.risk: Becomes costume if tag holes, string or tape textures leak into controls; the world must stay in type, colour and the chain.

raised.raise: The type ramp carries hierarchy; boxes are removed wherever a rule and a weight change suffice.
The focused exhibit stays at full ink while the rest of the chain drops back.
Every artifact carries a sequential number (case EX-, exhibit S1, approval AP-), and the numbers are how you navigate.
All figures are tabular monospace at full density: latency, tokens and scores are never rounded into prose.

options.label: Flight Strips
options.lineage: air-traffic flight progress strips in strip bays
options.thesis: Each run is a strip in a bay; a human clearance moves it on.
options.viewport: Dark bay ground; runs as colour-coded strips grouped by state, the selected strip expanded into its trace.
options.risk: The most familiar mapping for an ops tool; strips drift toward a kanban board and buff stock toward the cream default.

options.label: Midnight Transit Diagram
options.lineage: metropolitan rail diagrams fired as enamel
options.thesis: The workflow as a line map: classify, plan, retrieve and verify are stations every run travels.
options.viewport: The graph and loop as two lines across the top, the live run lit station by station, answer below.
options.case: Holds product clarity (the pipeline is literally a line), loses on audience fit: the dark mural fights screen-share and dense tables.
options.risk: A map that becomes the page instead of a signature move.

options.label: Jet-age Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: A run is a coupon book: each step tears off in sequence, and nothing disappears, it is voided.
options.viewport: Navy header; the run's steps as tabbed coupons, rejected approvals stamped VOID, the answer on the final coupon.
options.case: Holds audience fit (audit trails never delete), narrower on clarity: coupons stretch thin over tables and charts.
options.risk: Navy, red and white reads airline-branded rather than product.

options.label: Metro Typographic Tiles
options.thesis: Giant cropped lowercase type is the interface.
options.case: Loses both axes: dense traces and tables do not survive poster-scale type.
options.kept: Type ramp carries hierarchy instead of boxes.

options.label: Streaming Title Wall
options.thesis: Rows of tiles; the focused one grows.
options.case: Loses both: runs have no artwork, and browsing is not the job.
options.kept: Focus keeps full ink while the rest dims.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Every artifact gets a catalog number.
options.case: Loses both: coded colour strips hide statuses operators must read instantly.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Pure black and white data at full density.
options.case: Loses both: no colour left for state, and strobing is hostile to a working tool.
options.kept: Tabular monospace figures at full density.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean developer-tool console, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, chat thread, trace panel: the arrangement every agent console ships.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
